answer.rationale: C2 confirms the low-cost primary vendor delivered sharp unit-cost cuts last cycle with accurate invoicing and no onboarding friction; C4 shows incumbents can be moved on price and terms at renewal when benchmarked. Together they justify switching primary to the low-cost vendor to hit the 18% mandate, while flagging that last cycle's savings are a sample not a guarantee. Because the assembly line is at 94% with no buffer, I'm framing the move as a small guarded test rather than a full cutover — start with a partial volume allocation, keep incumbent on a short tail for continuity, and only scale once delivery performance holds. Cost is the primary lever; delivery risk is the binding constraint, so the guarded ramp is the defensible posture.
